newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa group applies for a Cape radio station.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa group applies for a Cape radio station.

text.p: South Africa's Cape FM consortium said on Thursday it had made an application for a license to the Independent Broadcasting Authority for a Cape Town radio station.

The consortium includes Mnyama Holdings, a Cape-based black empowerment group, with a 40 percent stake, Boland Financial Services, a part of Boland Bank Ltd, with a 35 percent stake and Dublin-based Radio Investments holding 20 percent.
"The consortium proposes a station called Cape FM Classic Hits which will have a distinct Cape flavour," the consortium said in a statement.
The station would offer a mix of soft and easy hits from the 60's to the 90's with a distinct Cape jazzy feel targeted at people between 20 and 45 years, the consortium said.
The projected listenership is 250,000 to 270,000 people daily and about 1.89 million people a week.
